title: Harvard–Anthropic–QuEra: Claude Mythos 5 Discovers 4×–39× Leaner Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
aiSystem: Claude Mythos 5 + OpenEvolve Evaluator (Anthropic / Harvard / QuEra)
whyItMatters: In a Harvard–Anthropic–QuEra study, Claude Mythos 5 in a closed evolutionary loop beat hand-crafted quantum circuits on 7 of 8 tasks—cutting Toffoli×qubit cost up to 39× (12× on DQI decoding, 17× on elliptic curves).
summary: Released on October 16, 2026 (highlighted by QuEra and Harvard on November 10, 2026), researchers from Harvard University (Mikhail Lukin, Susanne Yelin), Anthropic, and QuEra Computing paired Claude Mythos 5 with the open-source evolutionary framework OpenEvolve and an independent classical circuit verifier to discover state-of-the-art fault-tolerant quantum circuits with zero human intervention between rounds. Across seven of eight core computational primitives, Claude reduced both Toffoli-gate counts and logical qubit footprints relative to best published human designs: cutting the DQI Reed–Solomon decoder from 5.1M to ~440K Toffoli gates (12×), reducing the quantum-chemistry Coulomb potential space-time metric 9.9×, discovering a reversible modular-inversion circuit for elliptic-curve addition with 17× fewer gates in a 53-hour run, and achieving a 39× space-time cost reduction on a fixed-point Gaussian (alongside a separate Oct 13 IBM Research AI agent finding a 204× faster QEC decoder for $299 of inference).
technicalHighlights: Beats best published human-crafted fault-tolerant quantum circuits on 7 of 8 benchmark primitives using closed-loop LLM evolutionary search (Claude Mythos 5 + OpenEvolve).
Cuts DQI Reed–Solomon optimization decoder Toffoli gates 12× (5.1M → 440K), chemistry Coulomb potential cost 9.9×, elliptic-curve modular inversion gates 17×, and Gaussian space-time cost 39×.
Every circuit was deterministically verified for exact functional equivalence and exact Toffoli/qubit counts by an independent classical evaluator.
caveats: Resource reductions are verified classical circuit designs for core algorithmic building blocks rather than executions on physical fault-tolerant quantum hardware; peer review is pending.

scoreRationale.foundational: Discovers genuinely novel reversible quantum algorithms and circuit architectures beating decades of hand-optimized fault-tolerant primitives.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly pulls forward the practical horizon of fault-tolerant quantum computing for chemistry, optimization, and cryptography.
scoreRationale.verification: All circuits are deterministically checked by an independent classical evaluator for functional correctness and exact gate/qubit budgets.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomous closed-loop runs (up to 53 hours) outperformed decades of specialist human circuit engineering across 7 of 8 tasks.
